subject: MSA / Order Form — service obligations & response ladder
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@altishealth.com>, Ben Rodriguez <ben.rodriguez@altisops.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — service obligations & response ladder

Hi Sara / Ben —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion attached are two items: 1) the MSA with our proposed SLA redlines highlighted, and 2) a draft uptime / response ladder we suggest for the Order Form (fast reference).

High-level asks from our side:
- We can accept a 99.9% regional uptime target for the managed service but we want the definition of "Downtime" limited to customer-impacting REST/streaming endpoints (see §4.2).
- Service credits should be capped at a monthly percentage (we propose 30% cap) and calculated on per-region usage, not global roll-ups.
- P1 response time: initial ack within 15 minutes and working status update every 1 hour until mitigation.
- Scheduled maintenance windows: prefer once-per-week 2-hour window with 72-hour notice; emergencies excluded with post-facto notice and rollback plan.

Can you confirm if these are acceptable to procurement/legal on your side? If not, please send counter redlines and we can coordinate an hour with legal to go line-by-line.

I'll loop in Marissa from Legal if we get counter redlines so she can weight in on language.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attach: Altis_MSA_Redlines_20260707.docx (docx, 58KB); OrderForm-Draft-uptime-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)

From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@altishealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Rodriguez <ben.rodriguez@altisops.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — service obligations & response ladder

Jordan —

Thanks for sending these over. Ben and I reviewed with our procurement lead. A few quick notes before we do a formal redline: 

- Altis can accept the 99.9% regional target for production-only endpoints, but we need clarification on the exclusion list (internal maintenance, scheduled DB migrations, and third-party infra incidents).
- The 30% cap on credits is something we expected; procurement will want a sliding cap tied to committed spend tiers (e.g., 30% for < $50k/mo, 20% for $50-200k, 10% > $200k).
- P1 ack + hourly updates is reasonable; however, initial mitigation ETA should be within 1 hour for infra-origin P1s — is that feasible operationally?
- For maintenance, we prefer bi-weekly 4-hour windows at low traffic times; smaller customers can be exempted by order form.

I'll attach our preliminary redline and procurement notes by EOD. If you can share Marissa's legal availability tomorrow, we can schedule a 30-min call to reconcile the MSA language.

— Sara
Sara Cho
VP, Infrastructure — Altis Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@altishealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — service obligations & response ladder

Sara — great, thanks.

Quick responses to your bullets:
- Exclusions: we will add explicit carveouts for third-party provider outages and customer misconfiguration; proposed wording will list categories rather than specific vendors so we don't re-open for every provider change.
- Sliding cap: understood — we'll propose a tiered credit cap in the Order Form that maps to committed spend bands. I'll attach an updated uptime matrix with the tiers.
- P1 mitigation ETA: operationally our SREs can commit to an initial mitigation ETA target of 1 hour for infra-origin P1s when dedicated capacity is reserved (i.e., Dedicated / Private deployments). For Hosted customers the ETA is best-effort; we can mark this distinction in the Order Form.
- Maintenance cadence: we prefer weekly 2-hour windows for patching and KV-cache compactions; open to bi-weekly 4-hour if Altis needs fewer disruptions — let's pick which one goes into the Order Form and capture a mechanism for customer opt-out.

Marissa — can you do a 30-min call tomorrow (Wed 7/8) at 10:00am PT to walk through Altis's redline? Sara indicated they'll send their marked-up MSA by EOD today.

Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Cho <sara.cho@altishealth.com>, Ben Rodriguez <ben.rodriguez@altisops.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA / Order Form — service obligations & response ladder

Looping in quick legal notes before the call: 

- Please ask Altis to annotate any suggested definitions for "Downtime" and "Service Unavailable" in their redline. Our preferred approach is a limited definition tied to the API endpoints and Customer-facing UI only.
- For credits: we should keep the monthly cap but add a carveout that credits cannot exceed charges for the affected service during that month (standard anti-refund clause).
- Response ladder: we'll accept the P1 ack / hourly updates language. For the remediation SLA (time to resolution) we will keep it as best-effort language but add an operational runbook requirement in the Order Form for customers with Dedicated tiers.
- Maintenance: legal will not agree to a bi-weekly 4-hour mandatory window without a downtime mitigation plan. If Altis wants less frequent windows, they must accept a slightly lower availability target or agree to prioritized patching windows.

I can do 10:00am PT tomorrow for a 30-min call. I'll prepare a short redline summary to keep the meeting scoped to the 3 items above.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Rodriguez <ben.rodriguez@altisops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sara Cho <sara.cho@altishealth.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — service obligations & response ladder

Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks for the clarity. We reviewed your notes internally and attached the Altis redline (Altis_MSA_Marked_20260707.docx). A couple of clarifications we want on the call:

1) If we accept weekly 2-hour windows, can Redwood guarantee no more than two emergency maintenance events per quarter that would cause user-visible interruptions?
2) On the credits cap: would Redwood consider a true-up clause where, if Altis exceeds the committed spend band mid-term, the cap is re-evaluated for subsequent months?

We'll be on the call at 10:00am PT and will have procurement + tech lead present.

Best,
Ben
